m: to review, look at again; to think better of
s: 事故が続いたことを受けて、工場では安全対策を一から（　　）ことになった。
en: After a series of accidents, the factory is going to review its safety measures from scratch.
why: 見直す: to look at something again and rethink it. After accidents you go over the safety rules from the start (一から).
見守る means to watch over someone or something as it goes on (子どもを見守る). Rules are not watched over 'from scratch'.
見送る means to see someone off, or to shelve a plan. Shelving safety rules after accidents makes no sense, and 一から does not go with it.
見逃す means to miss seeing something, or to let a fault go. Nobody decides to miss rules on purpose.
tell: Going over something again to fix it: 見直す. 一から見直す, 計画を見直す.

s: この町では十年以上前から、住民と市が協力してごみの削減に（　　）いる。
en: In this town, residents and the city have been working together to cut waste for more than ten years.
why: 取り組む: to work hard on a problem or goal over time, with に: 削減に取り組む, 問題に取り組む.
取り込む means to take something in (洗濯物を取り込む, data, ideas), and 取り込んでいる can mean 'busy, in a rush'. Neither works with 削減に.
取り次ぐ means to pass a message or call on to someone else (電話を取り次ぐ). Nothing is being passed on.
取り締まる means to crack down on wrongdoing, with を (違反を取り締まる). Cutting waste is a goal, not an offence.
tell: Working steadily on a problem or goal: 〜に取り組む.

s: 長い間一人で悩んでいたことを、思い切って親友に（　　）。
en: I plucked up the courage and told my best friend about something I had been worrying about alone for a long time.
why: 打ち明ける: to tell someone a secret or worry you have kept to yourself. 思い切って and 親友に point to it.
打ち消す means to deny or cancel out (うわさを打ち消す). You do not deny a worry to a friend.
打ち出す means to put forward a plan or policy in public (方針を打ち出す). It is not used for telling a friend something private.
打ち切る means to cut something off before its end (連載を打ち切る). Nothing is being ended, and it does not take 親友に.
tell: Telling someone a secret or worry you kept inside: 打ち明ける. 悩みを打ち明ける.

m: to take on, agree to do
s: 忙しい時期だったが、お世話になっている先輩の頼みなので、その仕事を（　　）ことにした。
en: It was a busy time, but the request came from a senior colleague who has always looked after me, so I decided to take the job on.
why: 引き受ける: to agree to take on a job or request. 頼み (a request) and ことにした point to saying yes.
引き止める means to stop someone from leaving (帰ろうとする客を引き止める). It is used for people, not work.
引き出す means to draw out money or someone's ability (預金を引き出す, 力を引き出す). It is not agreeing to a task.
引き返す means to turn back the way you came. It takes no object like 仕事を.
tell: Saying yes to a job or request: 引き受ける. 仕事を引き受ける, 役を引き受ける.

m: to hold in your arms; to have (a problem) on your hands
s: 地方の多くの中小企業が、人手不足という深刻な問題を（　　）いる。
en: Many small and mid-sized companies in the regions are facing a serious problem: a shortage of workers.
why: 抱える: to hold in your arms, and so to have a problem or burden on your hands. 問題を抱える is the set phrase.
支える means to hold up or support (家族を支える). Nobody supports a problem.
構える means to set up a shop or home, or to take a stance (店を構える). It does not go with 問題.
蓄える means to save up money or strength for later (資金を蓄える). A problem is not saved up.
tell: Having a problem or worry on your hands: 問題を抱える, 悩みを抱える.

m: to inquire, contact someone to ask
s: 注文した商品が一週間たってもまだ届かないので、メールで店に（　　）。
en: The item I ordered still hadn't arrived after a week, so I emailed the shop to ask about it.
why: 問い合わせる: to contact someone to ask for information. A late order is a reason to ask the shop: 店に問い合わせる.
申し込む means to apply or sign up for something (講座に申し込む). You are asking about a parcel, not applying.
打ち合わせる means to go over plans together, with と (客と打ち合わせる). A parcel that has not come is not a meeting.
言い付ける means to give someone an order, or to tell on someone (先生に言い付ける). A late parcel calls for a question, not either of those.
tell: Contacting someone to ask about something: 〜に問い合わせる. 店に問い合わせる.

s: 部員全員が力を合わせて、大会までのいくつもの困難を（　　）。
en: All the club members pulled together and got through one difficulty after another on the way to the tournament.
why: 乗り越える: to climb over, and so to get through a hardship. 困難を乗り越える is the set phrase.
乗り換える means to change trains or switch to something else (電車を乗り換える). You do not switch hardships.
乗り遅れる means to miss a train or a trend, with に (終電に乗り遅れる). It does not take 困難を.
乗り出す means to set out on a new venture, with に (海外進出に乗り出す), or to lean forward. It does not take 困難を.
tell: Getting through a hardship: 困難を乗り越える, 壁を乗り越える.

m: to be full of energy, be eager
s: 新しいプロジェクトのリーダーに選ばれて、彼は朝から（　　）いる。
en: He has been picked to lead the new project, and he has been full of energy since the morning.
why: 張り切る: to be full of energy and eager to get going. Being picked as leader is a reason to be fired up.
思い切る means to make a bold decision, or to give up on something. It is used as 思い切って + verb, not as a state.
締め切る means to close a door, or to close applications at a deadline. A person is not 'closed' by a new role.
使い切る means to use something up completely (お金を使い切る). It needs an object and says nothing about mood.
tell: Fired up and eager, often before a new task: 張り切る. 張り切って準備する.

s: 電力不足が心配されるため、市は住民に節電への協力を（　　）いる。
en: Because a power shortage is feared, the city is calling on residents to help by saving electricity.
why: 呼びかける: to call on people, often the public, to do something. 協力を呼びかける is the set phrase in the news.
呼び止める means to call out to someone to make them stop (警官に呼び止められる). It does not take 協力を.
呼び出す means to call someone to come to a place (職員室に呼び出す), or to page them. Help is not summoned this way.
呼び寄せる means to bring someone to where you are (家族を呼び寄せる). It is used for people, not for help.
tell: Asking the public to do something: 〜に協力を呼びかける, 注意を呼びかける.

m: to master (a tool), use with full skill
s: 祖父は八十歳になるが、買ったばかりのスマートフォンをもう上手に（　　）いる。
en: My grandfather is eighty, but he is already handling the smartphone he just bought like an expert.
why: 使いこなす: to use a tool fully and with skill. 上手に and 'already, at eighty' point to mastering it.
使い分ける means to pick between several things to suit each purpose (敬語を使い分ける). One phone gives nothing to choose between.
使い捨てる means to throw something away after use (使い捨てのカップ). Nobody throws away a new phone 'skilfully'.
使い果たす means to use up money or strength until none is left (貯金を使い果たす). It is not used for a device.
tell: Using a tool with full skill: 使いこなす. Choosing between tools: 使い分ける.

m: to disturb, get in the way of
s: 夜中まで続く工事の音が、近くに住む人々の眠りを（　　）いる。
en: Construction noise that goes on into the middle of the night is disturbing the sleep of people who live nearby.
why: 妨げる: to get in the way of something so it cannot go on smoothly. Noise that breaks sleep is 眠りを妨げる.
防ぐ means to stop something bad from happening, or to guard against it (事故を防ぐ). Sleep is not something bad, and the noise is guarding no one.
塞ぐ means to block an opening or a path (穴を塞ぐ, 道を塞ぐ). Sleep is not a hole or a road.
断る means to say no to a request or offer. Noise cannot turn down sleep.
tell: Getting in the way of something good: 眠りを妨げる, 通行を妨げる. Stopping something bad: 防ぐ.

m: to be blessed with, be lucky to have
s: 旅行中の三日間は天気に（　　）、毎日海で泳ぐことができた。
en: We were lucky with the weather for all three days of the trip, so we could swim in the sea every day.
why: 恵まれる: to be blessed with something good, with に (天気に恵まれる, 才能に恵まれる). Good weather made the swimming possible.
頼まれる means to be asked to do something. Weather cannot ask anyone.
任される means to be put in charge of a job (仕事を任される). Weather does not hand out jobs.
囲まれる means to be surrounded by (自然に囲まれる). You can be surrounded by nature, but not by weather.
tell: Lucky to have something good: 〜に恵まれる. 天気に恵まれる, 人に恵まれる.

s: 大学で学んだ知識を（　　）、将来は地元の企業で働きたいと考えている。
en: I want to put what I learned at university to good use and work for a local company in the future.
why: 生かす: to make good use of a skill or what you know. 知識を生かす, 経験を生かす are set phrases.
生やす means to grow hair or a beard (ひげを生やす). It is not used for knowledge.
生じる means a problem or change comes about (問題が生じる). It takes no object, so 知識を生じて is not Japanese.
生み出す means to create something new (新しい商品を生み出す). Knowledge you have already learned is not created again.
tell: Putting a skill or knowledge to good use: 知識を生かす, 経験を生かす.

s: 週末に子どもたちが遊んだあと、リビングがひどく（　　）いた。
en: After the children had been playing at the weekend, the living room was a terrible mess.
why: 散らかる: a place is messy with things left all over it. The subject is the room: 部屋が散らかる.
散らばる means the things themselves are scattered (おもちゃが散らばる). The room cannot be the subject.
崩れる means something falls apart or collapses (山が崩れる). Play does not make a room collapse.
ずれる means something slips out of place or out of line (時間がずれる). It is not used for a whole room.
tell: A place is messy: 部屋が散らかる. The things are scattered: 物が散らばる.

s: 自分の考えを相手に（　　）ばかりでは、話し合いはうまくいかない。
en: If you only push your own ideas onto the other person, a discussion will not go well.
why: 押し付ける: to force your idea, job or blame on someone else, with を and に (考えを人に押し付ける).
押しかける means to turn up somewhere uninvited (家に押しかける). It takes no object like 考えを.
押し切る means to push ahead in spite of opposition (反対を押し切る). Its object is the opposition, and it does not take 相手に.
押し込む means to cram a thing into a space (かばんに服を押し込む). Ideas are not stuffed into a person.
tell: Forcing something on someone: AをBに押し付ける. 考え, 仕事, 責任を押し付ける.

s: 失敗したことはもう忘れて、気持ちを（　　）次の仕事に取りかかろう。
en: Forget about the mistake now, switch your mindset, and let's get on with the next job.
why: 切り替える: to switch from one mode or state to another. 気持ちを切り替える means putting a setback behind you and moving on.
取り替える means to swap one object for another (電池を取り替える). Feelings are not swapped like parts.
言い換える means to say the same thing in other words. Nothing is being reworded.
着替える means to change your clothes. It is only used for clothes.
tell: Switching mood or mode: 気持ちを切り替える, 画面を切り替える. Swapping a part: 取り替える.

s: 友達との話に夢中になっていて、（　　）降りる駅を通り過ぎてしまった。
en: I was so caught up talking with my friend that I carelessly went right past my stop.
why: うっかり: without paying attention, so you make a slip. Being lost in talk and てしまった fit a careless mistake.
こっそり means secretly, so no one notices. Missing your stop was not done on purpose.
がっかり means disappointed, and goes with する (結果にがっかりする). It does not describe how you missed a stop.
ゆったり means roomy or relaxed (ゆったりした服). It says nothing about a slip.
tell: A careless slip: うっかり〜てしまう. うっかり忘れる, うっかり乗り過ごす.

s: 好きな仕事に就いてから、姉は毎日（　　）していて、表情も明るくなった。
en: Since she started a job she loves, my sister has been full of life every day, and she looks much brighter too.
why: いきいき: full of life and energy. A job she loves and a brighter face both point to it.
いらいら means irritated and on edge. That does not go with a brighter face.
うとうと means dozing off. It does not fit someone thriving in a job she loves.
ぶらぶら means wandering around, or idling with nothing to do. She has just started a job.
tell: Full of life and energy: いきいき(と)する, いきいきと働く.

s: スーツケースに荷物が（　　）詰まっていて、もう何も入らない。
en: The suitcase is packed solid with luggage, and nothing else will fit.
why: ぎっしり: packed tight, with no gaps. It goes with 詰まる and 並ぶ: ぎっしり詰まる.
ぐっすり means sleeping deeply (ぐっすり眠る). It is only used for sleep.
びっしょり means soaking wet (汗でびっしょり). A full suitcase is not wet.
すっきり means neat and clear, or refreshed. A case too full to take more is the opposite.
tell: Packed tight with no room left: ぎっしり詰まる, 予定がぎっしり.

s: 体育館に集まった保護者は、（　　）数えて三百人ほどだった。
en: At a rough count, about three hundred parents had gathered in the gym.
why: ざっと: roughly, without going into detail. It goes with a rough count and ほど: ざっと数えて三百人ほど.
ぴったり means exactly. That clashes with ほど, which says the number is only rough.
きっと means 'surely', for a guess about what will happen (きっと晴れる). It cannot describe how you counted.
ほっと means relieved (ほっとする). It describes a feeling, not a way of counting.
tell: A rough count or a quick look: ざっと数える, ざっと目を通す. Exact is ぴったり.

m: taking the trouble, going out of your way
s: お忙しいところ、遠くから（　　）お越しいただき、ありがとうございます。
en: Thank you for taking the trouble to come all this way when you are so busy.
why: わざわざ: going out of your way to do something for someone. It goes with thanks: わざわざ来ていただいて.
わざと means on purpose, usually for something bad (わざと負ける). It does not go with thanks.
ついでに means while you are at it, on the way to something else. Coming 遠くから is the opposite of a side trip.
たまたま means by chance. You would not thank a guest for coming a long way by accident.
tell: Taking the trouble, often in thanks: わざわざ. On purpose, often for something bad: わざと.

m: at last, finally (the awaited moment is here)
s: 三年かけて準備してきた新しい駅ビルが、（　　）明日オープンする。
en: The new station building, three years in the making, finally opens tomorrow.
why: いよいよ: at last, the long-awaited moment is here or very near. It fits a big opening after three years of work.
ますます means more and more (ますます寒くなる). An opening day does not grow.
せいぜい means at most, or doing what little you can (せいぜい千円だ). It does not mark a moment.
たびたび means often, again and again. A building opens once.
tell: The long-awaited moment has come: いよいよ明日, いよいよ本番. More and more: ますます.

s: 久しぶりに故郷に帰り、家族のありがたさを（　　）感じた。
en: Going back to my hometown after a long time, I felt deep down how lucky I am to have my family.
why: しみじみ: feeling something deeply and quietly, from the heart. It goes with 感じる and 思う about family, age or the past.
はらはら means anxious while watching something risky (試合をはらはらしながら見る). Gratitude is not anxiety.
ぞくぞく means shivers, from cold, fear or excitement. It is a body feeling, not quiet thanks.
ひやひや means nervous that something will go wrong (ばれないかひやひやする). It does not fit gratitude.
tell: Feeling something deeply and quietly: しみじみ(と)感じる, しみじみ思う.

s: どう考えても無理な頼みだったので、その場で（　　）断った。
en: It was an impossible request however you looked at it, so I turned it down flatly on the spot.
why: きっぱり: clearly and firmly, leaving no doubt. It goes with 断る, やめる and 言う.
ぴったり means exactly right, or fitting perfectly (サイズがぴったり). It does not describe a firm no.
ばったり means running into someone by chance (友人にばったり会う), or falling down suddenly.
すっきり means neat, clear or refreshed (気分がすっきりする). It is not a way of refusing.
tell: A clear, firm no: きっぱり断る, きっぱりやめる.

s: 子どもが急に道に飛び出してきたので、運転手は（　　）ブレーキを踏んだ。
en: A child suddenly ran out into the road, and the driver hit the brakes on reflex.
why: とっさに: in an instant, with no time to think. A child running out makes the driver react on reflex.
やけに means oddly or unusually (今日はやけに静かだ). It describes a state, not a quick reaction.
いまに means before long, about the future (いまに分かる). The braking has already happened.
めったに means rarely, and it needs a negative (めったにない). The sentence is about one quick reaction, not how often.
tell: Reacting in an instant, with no time to think: とっさに. とっさに手を出す, とっさに隠れる.

s: 新人の山田さんは、頼まれた仕事をいつも（　　）片付けるので、みんなに信頼されている。
en: Yamada, our new hire, always gets through the work she is given quickly and efficiently, so everyone trusts her.
why: てきぱき: doing work quickly and efficiently, with no wasted moves. It goes with 片付ける and 働く, and earns trust.
はきはき means speaking clearly and confidently (はきはき答える). It is about how you talk, not how you work.
のろのろ means slowly and sluggishly. Slow work would not make everyone trust her.
ばらばら means scattered or in pieces (意見がばらばらだ). It does not describe a way of working.
tell: Quick, efficient work: てきぱき. Clear, confident speech: はきはき.

s: この施設では、お年寄りや車いすの人への（　　）から、入り口の段差をなくした。
en: Out of consideration for elderly people and wheelchair users, this facility removed the step at its entrance.
why: 配慮: care and thought for other people's needs, which leads to action. 〜への配慮から means 'out of consideration for'.
遠慮 means holding back out of regard for others (遠慮して言わない). Here the facility acted; it did not hold back.
配分 means sharing out money, time or work (予算の配分). Nothing is being shared out here.
注目 means attention or notice (注目を集める). Watching people closely is not a reason to remove a step.
tell: Thought for others that leads to action: 配慮. Holding back for others: 遠慮.

s: 工事が順調に進んでいるため、新しい橋は予定より早く完成する（　　）だ。
en: Work is going smoothly, so the new bridge is expected to be finished ahead of schedule.
why: 見込み: an expectation based on how things are going. 〜する見込みだ is how the news says 'is expected to'.
見本 means a sample or model to look at (商品の見本). It cannot follow 完成する.
見出し means a headline or heading (新聞の見出し). It is not a forecast.
見学 means a visit to see how something works (工場見学). It is not a forecast either.
tell: A forecast in the news: 〜する見込みだ, 〜見込みがない. A sample is 見本.

s: 試合に勝っていても、最後の一秒まで（　　）してはいけない。
en: Even when you are winning, you must not let your guard down until the very last second.
why: 油断: dropping your guard because you feel safe. Being ahead is exactly when people do it: 油断してはいけない.
我慢 means putting up with something hard. Telling a winning side not to endure makes no sense.
退屈 means being bored. The warning is about carelessness, not boredom.
反省 means looking back on your own mistakes. It is not a danger while you are winning.
tell: Dropping your guard because things look safe: 油断する. 油断大敵.

s: 出張で使うホテルと新幹線の切符は、総務部が（　　）してくれる。
en: The general affairs department books the hotels and bullet train tickets we need for business trips.
why: 手配: arranging what is needed, such as tickets, rooms or cars. 切符を手配する, ホテルを手配する.
手入れ means looking after something to keep it in good shape (庭の手入れ, 肌の手入れ). Tickets are not maintained.
手直し means fixing small faults in finished work (原稿を手直しする). Nothing here needs fixing.
手出し means meddling, or making the first move in a fight. It is never a service someone does for you.
tell: Booking or arranging what is needed: 手配する. ホテル, 車, 切符を手配する.

s: 彼の主張には、はっきりとした（　　）がないので、信じることはできない。
en: His claim has no clear basis, so I cannot believe it.
why: 根拠: the facts or reasons that back up a claim. 主張 and 信じることはできない point to missing evidence.
原因 means the cause of an event (事故の原因). A claim needs support, not a cause.
根気 means patience and staying power (根気がいる仕事). It is about people, not claims.
起源 means the origin of something old (文明の起源). A claim's backing is not its origin.
tell: The facts behind a claim: 根拠. 根拠がない, 根拠を示す. The cause of an event: 原因.

s: 我が家では、料理や掃除などの家事を夫婦で（　　）している。
en: In our home, my husband and I share the housework, such as cooking and cleaning.
why: 分担: splitting work so each person takes a part. 家事を分担する, 費用を分担する.
分解 means taking a machine apart (時計を分解する). Chores are not taken apart.
分析 means studying something closely by breaking it down (データを分析する). Doing chores is not studying them.
分別 (ぶんべつ) means sorting things such as rubbish into types (ごみを分別する). Chores are shared, not sorted.
tell: Each person taking a part of the work: 分担する. 家事を分担する.

s: 新しく来た部長は、まず各部署の現状を（　　）することから始めた。
en: The new department head began by getting a clear picture of where each section stood.
why: 把握: getting a full and accurate grasp of a situation. 現状を把握する is the set phrase at work.
確保 means securing something you need, such as seats, staff or money (人員を確保する). The present state of things is not secured.
獲得 means winning or gaining something through effort (メダルを獲得する). A situation is not won.
採用 means hiring a person or adopting an idea (新人を採用する). It does not fit looking into a situation.
tell: Getting a clear grasp of a situation: 把握する. 現状を把握する, 状況を把握する.

s: 狭い部屋でも、収納の仕方を（　　）すれば、ずいぶん広く使える。
en: Even in a small room, if you get creative with how you store things, you can use the space much more freely.
why: 工夫: thinking up a clever way to do something better. 仕方を工夫する is the usual pair.
工事 means construction work on a road or building. Changing how you store things is not building work.
加工 means processing a material into a product (木材を加工する). A way of storing is not a material.
工作 means making things by hand, as in a school craft class, or plotting behind the scenes. Neither fits.
tell: Thinking up a better way: 工夫する. 〜の仕方を工夫する.

s: この病院には、看護師として三十年以上働いている（　　）が何人もいる。
en: This hospital has several veterans who have worked as nurses for over thirty years.
why: ベテラン: someone with long experience in their job. Thirty years as a nurse is the cue.
アマチュア means an amateur who does something as a hobby. A nurse working for thirty years is a professional.
ゲスト means a guest, for example on a TV show. Staff who work at a hospital are not guests.
ファン means a fan of a team or singer. It has nothing to do with years at work.
tell: Someone with long experience at their job: ベテラン. ベテランの職人, ベテラン社員.

s: この化粧品は、二十代の働く女性を（　　）にして開発された。
en: This cosmetics line was developed with working women in their twenties as its target.
why: ターゲット: the group of people a product or campaign is aimed at. 〜をターゲットにする.
ゴール means a goal: the finish line, or an aim you reach. Customers are not a finish line.
ポイント means a key point, or points on a card. It does not name who a product is for.
ターミナル means a terminal: a station or airport building where routes meet. It has nothing to do with customers.
tell: The group something is aimed at: ターゲット. 若者をターゲットにした商品.

s: 面接では、自分の長所やこれまでの経験をうまく（　　）することが大切だ。
en: In a job interview, it is important to present your strengths and past experience well.
why: アピール: putting your good points forward so others notice them. 長所をアピールする is the interview phrase.
アドバイス means advice you give someone else. You do not advise your own strengths.
アナウンス means an announcement over a speaker, as at a station. It is not how you sell yourself.
リクエスト means a request, such as for a song. Strengths are shown, not requested.
tell: Showing your good points so others notice: アピールする. 長所をアピールする.

s: 謝ろうと思っていたが、（　　）が悪くて、なかなか話しかけられなかった。
en: I meant to apologise, but the timing was never right, so I could not bring myself to speak to her.
why: タイミング: the right moment to do something. タイミングが悪い means it never felt like the right moment.
バランス means balance between things (栄養のバランス). It has nothing to do with when to speak.
スピード means speed. It is fast or slow, not a moment for starting a talk.
レベル means a level or standard (レベルが高い). It does not describe a moment.
tell: The right moment: タイミングがいい, タイミングが悪い, タイミングを見る.

s: サッカーの試合は前半を終えて、日本チームが二対〇で（　　）している。
en: At half-time in the football match, Japan is leading two to nil.
why: リード: being ahead in a match or race. 二対〇でリードする means being two goals up.
オーバー means going over a limit (予算をオーバーする). A score is not a limit.
カバー means covering for someone or something (ミスをカバーする). It does not describe the score.
パス means passing the ball, or passing a test. It does not tell you who is ahead.
tell: Being ahead in a game: リードする. 二点リード, 大きくリードする.

s: この水筒は、冷たい飲み物の温度を半日ほど（　　）することができる。
en: This flask can hold a cold drink at the same temperature for about half a day.
why: キープ: keeping something in the same state, or holding on to it. 温度をキープする, 席をキープする.
ストップ means stopping something that is moving (作業をストップする). A temperature is held, not stopped.
チェンジ means changing one thing for another. A flask's job is the opposite: no change.
カット means cutting or reducing (費用をカットする). A flask does not cut the temperature.
tell: Keeping something as it is: キープする. 温度, ペース, 席をキープする.
